title.name: Bazaar Basra
title.tagline: One year at the market stall

prologue: Basra, in the year 638. The city is new, built of reed and mud brick where the rivers meet.
Your uncle hands you his market stall and his ledger, then leaves on a long journey.
His note: "Keep honest weights. Write down every cost. At the end of the year, count what you own."
The crier reads a letter from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): value your trade goods each year and pay zakat on them. (Paraphrase)
You have 160 dirham, two baskets of dates and a roll of cloth. One lunar year starts now.

stall.title: Rent a stall for the week
stall.loan: Short of rent. Your uncle's friend lends {n} dirham, interest free (qard hasan).

alley.title: The alleys of Basra

arrive.market: The bazaar entrance. Your stall is waiting.
arrive.gate: The city gate. Caravans to the groves and the port leave from here.
arrive.bayt: The bayt al-mal. Zakat is counted and paid here at the end of the year.

alley.notYet: Come back at the end of the year.

source.title: Where will you buy this weekend?
source.crier2: The crier: a ship from India has docked at Ubulla. Spices are cheap this week.
source.crier3: A Bedouin trader camps outside the gate. He offers leather on credit.
source.crier4: Winter is coming. Cloth will sell well in the cold.

buy.title: Buy and pack
buy.hint: Buy, then tap a good and tap the cart to pack it.
buy.padNote: A jar touching cloth or straw will not break.

ride.title: The ride home
ride.broken: {n} jar cracked on the road. Straw would have saved it.
ride.brokenMany: {n} jars cracked on the road. Straw would have saved them.

weekendLedger.title: Weekend ledger
weekendLedger.credit: Bought on credit, owed at year end
weekendLedger.note: Landed cost is your floor price. Sell above it.

shop.setup: Set your prices, then open the stall.
shop.inspector: The market inspector checked your scale. The stall opens at midday.
shop.crierCaravan: The crier: a caravan is late. Dates are short today.
shop.crierHarith: Hoarding food to raise its price (ihtikar) is forbidden.
shop.crierEnd: The crier: the year is over. Count what you own.
shop.rest: Nothing to sell today. Close the stall

scale.title: A customer asks by weight
scale.hint: Hold to fill the pan. Let go at the line.
scale.over: Too much. You gave stock away.

harith.title: Harith leans over your stall
harith.body: "The caravan is late. Hold your dates until tomorrow and sell them dear."
harith.fairOutcome: You sold fairly. Word spreads, and a regular comes each day.
harith.holdOutcome: The inspector saw the empty shelf. The caravan came in the night, and dates are cheap now.

bayt.title: The bayt al-mal
bayt.clerk: The clerk opens your ledger. "Let us count what you own today."
bayt.valueHint: Pick the price for each stack.
bayt.wrongPaid: Not what you paid. Trade goods are valued at today's market price.
bayt.wrongHoped: Not what you hope to get. Use the price the market pays today.
bayt.noStock: Your storeroom is empty. Nothing to value.
bayt.under: You are under the nisab. No zakat is due this year.
bayt.paid: The clerk writes your zakat in his register.
bayt.sadaqahBody: Zakat is paid. Would you like to give extra, by choice?

asnaf.title: Where zakat goes
scenes: A widow with no income receives food for the month.
A labourer who works but cannot cover his rent gets help.
The clerk himself is paid for his work.
A Persian craftsman, new to Islam, is helped to settle in the city.
A man pays to buy back his freedom.
A boatman whose boat sank has his debt cleared.
Support for good works for the community.
A traveller robbed on the road gets enough to reach home.
asnaf.others: Other traders' zakat did this work this year.

end.title: Your year
end.line: Zakat on trade goods is still due today. Count yours.
end.shareText: My year at the Basra bazaar: {profit} dirham profit, amanah {amanah}, {zakat} dirham zakat paid.
